situation.person: Nigerian mother between 6 weeks and 6 months postpartum, at home and in diaspora, with a two-to-three-finger gap above the navel, who cannot lift her toddler without coning and pain
situation.specific_situation: Her belly cones and bulges whenever she sits up or laughs, so she avoids movement entirely or repeats the crunches that made the ridge worse. Without a progression she cannot trust her own body, and she cannot pick up her own child.
situation.trigger: The six-week check named the gap, then a video reel and an owambe photo made the pooch impossible to ignore.
situation.problem: No safe progression exists, therefore she either does nothing and weakens further, or repeats harmful exercise.
situation.failed_attempt: Tried a waist trainer that worsened breathing with no change, detox teas suspected fake, and crunches and sit-ups that raised a ridge, so she stopped everything; the nurse offered no plan.

situation.desired_transformation: She can brace, lift and move without coning, and the finger-width number trends down; the progression chart is posted and followed.

evidence.claim: Postpartum runners with pelvic-floor symptoms should be referred to a specialised professional before progressing to impact; heaviness, leaking, visible gap, pelvic pain and bleeding beyond 8 weeks are referral signals.
Intra-abdominal-pressure management with pelvic-floor co-activation is the rationale for the precautionary avoid-list; individual avoid-items are consensus caution, not RCT-proven harm.
